- Integrations: event pipeline into their infra, want private deployment later but starting hosted API.
- Expected token volumes: you mentioned average ~300M tokens/month with peaks to ~600M during launches.
- Primary goals: predictable unit economics, lower per-token cost for steady state, and clear procurement path for startup credits.

Action items I took away:
1) I’ll send a simple pricing breakdown (baseline hosted + committed-use tiers + startup program details).
2) Share an MOP (mutual action plan) to surface procurement milestones.
3) Follow up with a formal quote and T&Cs if this looks like the right direction.

I attached a quick pricing calc so you can tweak volumes. High-level questions for you: could you confirm target $/1M token target for procurement review and whether NovaFlow qualifies for a startup program (YC or seed stage)? Also, who will be the procurement contact (cc’d Carlos?)

- Volumes: the 300M was our conservative steady-state. Our internal plan assumes ~450M tokens/month in Q1 post-launch, with peaks ~900M for big events (we can provide a month-by-month forecast).
- Budget: procurement is looking for a target range of $1,500–$4,000/month initially, scaling up. We’re focused on $/1M tokens closer to $5–$8 if possible.

Subject: Re: Pricing & committed-use discount follow-up (NovaFlow)

Emma — perfect, thanks for the detail. Below is a concise pricing & discount summary based on the volumes you called out. I’ve also attached an updated pricing calc and an initial Mutual Action Plan (MAP).

Baseline hosted (pay-as-you-go):
- List: $10.00 per 1M tokens (generation + embedding blended estimate).

Committed-use (prepaid monthly / annualized) examples:
- 12-month commitment (tier A: 300M tokens/mo): 25% off -> $7.50 /1M tokens.
- 24-month commitment (tier B: 450M tokens/mo): 35% off -> $6.50 /1M tokens.
- 36-month (high commitment): 40% off -> $6.00 /1M tokens + priority capacity allocation.

Startup program (NovaFlow eligible):
- One-year starter credit: 50% credit on invoices up to $120k in first 12 months (available to seed-stage startups with proof).
- Credits apply to hosted invoice after committed-use discounts; they reduce the invoice but do not change contracted rates.

Multi-year incentives:
- Additional 5% incentive for signed multi-year contracts (applies on top of committed-use discounts for 24+ month deals).
- Example: 24-month tier B effective rate -> $6.50 - 5% = $6.175 /1M tokens.

Unit economics worked example (your steady-state + Q1 scale):
- Scenario A (steady-state 450M tokens/mo, 24-mo commitment at effective $6.175):
  - Monthly cost = 450 * $6.175 = $2,778.75
  - Annual = ~$33,345
- Scenario B (peaks 900M tokens/mo but average 600M): if you use burst capacity above committed amount, burst billed at list or negotiated burst rate; we can include burst protection in the contract.

Notes / flexibility:
- We can structure a ramp in the MAP (month-to-month true-ups) to avoid over-commit at launch.
- Startup credit is a billing credit applied after discounts (not multiplicative). We can discuss alternative structures if procurement prefers net-rate guarantees.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll prepare a formal quote + SOW + standard T&Cs for Carlos and your procurement team.
2) Sign MAP to lock milestones and ramp.
3) Legal/procurement review (we can accommodate a one negotiated change list).

I attached: redwood_pricing_calc.xlsx (updated), mutual_action_plan.docx. Would you like me to propose a draft quote by EOD tomorrow?

—
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
